text:
maria: heads-up — i just imported the staging RDS secret from the sops export and now `terraform plan` is failing with a tainted secret + state lock error. anyone seen this combo before? :eyes:
kevin: can you paste the exact `terraform plan` output (the error block)?
maria: sure — here's the relevant tail:
```
Error: Error refreshing state: 1 error(s) occurred:
	* provider registry.terraform.io/hashicorp/aws: error while locking state: timeout waiting for state lock (ID: 5f3b8c8a)

Releasing state lock. If necessary run: terraform force-unlock 5f3b8c8a

# module.db.aws_secretsmanager_secret_version.secret[0] is tainted
  + resource will be created
```
olga: ok two things to check: is the lock actually active in the Dynamo table (we use s3+ddb backend for staging)? sometimes an interrupted import leaves a stale lock.
kevin: +1. if the lock is stale, `terraform force-unlock 5f3b8c8a` will clear it. but double-check no one is running an apply.
samir: also: after you clear the lock, run `terraform plan -refresh-only` first to get state back in sync before a normal plan. importing secrets can leave secret_version resources in an odd state.
maria: we're on workspace `staging` and i just confirmed no active CI runs. i can force-unlock but want to avoid making things worse.
kevin: another possible cause — we recently switched the aws provider alias for the db module (provider change -> provider address replaced). if the provider address changed, terraform sometimes marks resources tainted. check `terraform state list | grep secret` and `terraform state show module.db.aws_secretsmanager_secret.secret[0]` to see provider meta.
olga: if provider mismatch is the cause, `terraform state replace-provider 'registry.terraform.io/-/aws' 'registry.terraform.io/hashicorp/aws'` (adjust addresses to match your state) will fix the provider address without recreating.
samir: if it's strictly the secret_version resource that's tainted (and it's safe to recreate), `terraform taint module.db.aws_secretsmanager_secret_version.secret[0]` then `terraform apply -target=module.db.aws_secretsmanager_secret_version.secret[0]` is a low-risk fix for staging. but proceed carefully for prod.
maria: thanks — plan for me: 1) check ddb lock entry 2) force-unlock if stale 3) `plan -refresh-only` 4) inspect provider address and either replace-provider or taint+apply. i'll report back.
kevin: if you hit the lock again, paste the full `terraform force-unlock` output. sometimes the backend returns a different lock id.
deploy-bot: CI:staging-terraform #842 queued (maria) :gear:  
samir: i can watch with you in case you need a hand — ping me when you run force-unlock.
maria: will do — thanks all :thumbsup:
